subject: Leadership call recap — outcomes, risks, and procurement lanes
messages:
From: jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com
To: Eleanor Park <eleanor.park@healthsync.com>, Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@healthsync.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-11-24T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Leadership call recap — outcomes, risks, and procurement lanes

Hi Eleanor / Tom — thanks again for taking the leadership call earlier today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. If I missed anything, please flag.

Highlights / business outcomes you emphasized:
- Reduce inference cost per 1M tokens by ~40% vs current on-prem setup while keeping P95 latency under 400ms for interactive workflows.
- Replace brittle in-house batching layer to reduce engineering operational load and free up 1 FTE for feature work.
- Pilot Redwood in a bounded environment (one model family, two endpoints) with a goal to measure cost/latency and evaluate quality drift.

Key risks you called out:
- Data residency for PHI-adjacent logs (audit trail requirement).
- SOC2 reporting and encryption-at-rest / KMS controls.
- Procurement timeline: need legal + security sign-off before Q1 pilot kick-off.

Proposed procurement lane and milestones:
1) Security review + evidence exchange (2 weeks) — we’ll share SOC2 artifacts and answer questionnaire.
2) Pilot SOW (2–3 weeks) — 6-week pilot with agreed success metrics; draft SOW attached.
3) Procurement & legal review (3–6 weeks) — target contract signature by end of Q1.

Immediate asks / owners:
- Eleanor: confirm procurement contact and preferred timeline (you mentioned a mid-Jan window)
- Tom: share any must-have success metrics for the pilot (cost target, latency P95, sample traffic profile)
- Marcus / Laura (cc): I’ve attached a draft SOW and the security spreadsheet you requested; Marcus will support the security questionnaire responses.

Attachments: HealthSync-SOW-draft-v1.pdf, HealthSync-security-questions.xlsx

Next meeting: propose 30 mins on Dec 8 to finalize pilot metrics and acceptance criteria. I’ll send a calendar invite if that works.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Eleanor Park <eleanor.park@healthsync.com>
To: jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com, Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@healthsync.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-11-25T10:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Leadership call recap — outcomes, risks, and procurement lanes

Thanks Jasmine — concise and helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Procurement contact: procurement@healthsync.com (CC’d on this reply). We expect an initial intake/qualification step with procurement the week of Dec 13.

2) Security / compliance: please send SOC2 Type II report and any architecture diagrams showing network segregation for private deployments. Attached is our standard security questionnaire (filled out by our security team) — I marked high-priority rows that need evidence.

3) Pilot success metrics: our engineering lead wants two things measured during pilot:
- Average cost per 1000 inference requests (we’ll provide the current baseline)
- P95 latency under 400ms for the representative 99th-percentile user flow

4) Timeline: mid-Jan kickoff sounds right, but procurement/legal may push the signature window into late Feb depending on redlines. If you have standard timelines for security review + SOW cycling, please call them out.

We’ll review the SOW and the security spreadsheet this week and give feedback by Nov 30.

Eleanor Park
VP Product Operations | HealthSync
eleanor.park@healthsync.com

> Hi Eleanor / Tom — thanks again for taking the leadership call earlier today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. If I missed anything, please flag.

From: jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com
To: Eleanor Park <eleanor.park@healthsync.com>, Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@healthsync.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-11-30T08:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Leadership call recap — outcomes, risks, and procurement lanes

Eleanor — thanks for the fast turn. Appreciate the procurement contact and the marked questionnaire. Quick notes in response: 

- SOC2 & architecture: Marcus will share our SOC2 Type II summary and a network/architecture diagram showing how Redwood Private can be deployed in a customer VPC with KMS control. Expect those by EOD Dec 1.
- SOW: I’ve attached a slightly revised SOW that shortens the pilot timeline to 5 weeks with an accelerated acceptance window (we can extend if you want). See the cover notes in the SOW for the success metrics we propose.
- Timeline: Typical cadence for customers who want a tight Q1 start is 3–6 weeks for security review + SOW negotiation, followed by procurement/legal (2–4 weeks). We’ll surface any redlines early.

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP) — quick version:
- Dec 1–8: Evidence exchange (SOC2, architecture, questionnaire responses) — owner: Marcus
- Dec 9–16: SOW finalization and signoff on pilot metrics — owner: Jasmine / Eleanor
- Jan 4–8: Pilot kickoff (if procurement sign-off achieved) — owner: HealthSync ops / Redwood PM

If that looks reasonable I’ll lock the Dec 8 meeting and circulate a calendar invite.

Attachments: HealthSync-SOW-draft-v1.pdf (updated)

Thanks,
Jasmine

Subject: Internal: HealthSync procurement gating and escalation items

Internal note (do not forward):

Summary of external asks and our immediate blockers:
- Security artifacts requested: SOC2 Type II, network diagram for Redwood Private, answers to the attached questionnaire.
- Procurement timeline: intake week of Dec 13; potential signature target late Feb.
- Pilot acceptance metrics: cost per 1000 requests & P95 latency target.

Action items for our team:
1) I will assemble the SOC2 summary + architecture diagram and send to Eleanor by EOD Dec 1 (done).
2) Legal: pre-seed standard SOW terms with Finance for any discount/credit ask. Jasmine, note their procurement may ask for a pilot credit — recommend we pre-authorize up to $10k credit for a 6-week pilot; Laura, can you confirm finance OK?
3) Escalation: if procurement pushes signing beyond Mar 1 we should escalate to the sales leader to request an enterprise pipeline prioritization slot.

I’ll join the Dec 8 sync as backup for technical security questions.

Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineering Lead | Redwood Inference
